mappings.preservedMeaning: The absence is explicit: the scoped AWS inventory does not contain a lifecycle-managed aggregate that contains compute nodes as one infrastructure unit.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: CloudFormation stack structure is outside the provider-native inventory scope, and neither an EC2 Fleet nor a load-balancer target group establishes the aggregate ownership and lifecycle semantics in this concept.

evidence.supports: No element in the pinned, scoped inventory is an infrastructure aggregate; this is an inventory/schema absence, not runtime proof.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The absence is explicit: no scoped native element simultaneously represents a named compute group, declares its size, and is selected collectively as a load-balancer backend.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: EC2 Fleet has target-capacity schema and TargetGroup has backend-target schema, but the pinned schema does not establish one shared group identity or a Fleet-to-TargetGroup relation; composing them would invent semantics.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes fleet capacity only; it does not establish collective load-balancer backend selection.

mappings.preservedMeaning: AWS::EC2::Instance is a lifecycle-managed VM compute resource whose schema selects capacity and an execution-environment image.

evidence.supports: The resource schema contains InstanceType and ImageId alongside instance provisioning properties.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A VPC provides a managed logical network boundary within which subnets and compute connectivity are placed.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The VPC schema is explicitly IP-oriented and includes CIDR and DNS behavior, so it is narrower and more bundled than a layer-neutral logical interconnection boundary.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes VPC identity with CIDR and DNS configuration candidates.

mappings.preservedMeaning: AWS::EC2::Subnet is an independently declared IP subnet with CIDR and VpcId placement inside a VPC.

evidence.supports: The schema identifies the subnet resource and exposes CidrBlock and VpcId.

mappings.preservedMeaning: Subnet properties carry an IP range and address-assignment choices used by connectivity in a VPC.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: AWS expresses these settings on an independently identified subnet rather than as composable configuration on an existing network; the schema does not expose the neutral concept's gateway setting as part of this resource.

evidence.supports: CidrBlock is schema evidence for the IP-range portion; MapPublicIpOnLaunch and AssignIpv6AddressOnCreation are allocation-related candidates.

mappings.preservedMeaning: NetworkInterfaceAttachment explicitly connects an instance and a network interface, while NetworkInterface carries subnet placement and per-interface addressing candidates.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Attachment identity and interface addressing are split across two resources, and primary-interface creation may instead be embedded in instance configuration; schema presence does not prove which form runtime provisioning requires.

evidence.supports: InstanceId and NetworkInterfaceId form an explicit attachment candidate.
SubnetId and private/IPv6 address properties provide interface placement and addressing candidates.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A security group is an assignable network-security policy object containing ingress and egress filtering rules and associated with a VPC.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes VpcId plus SecurityGroupIngress and SecurityGroupEgress rule collections.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The two direction-specific resource types express protocol, port range, network prefix or peer group, and the containing security group.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Direction is represented by distinct ingress and egress resource types rather than a rule field; action, priority, and independent statefulness controls are not present in these schemas.

evidence.supports: Ingress rule schema exposes IpProtocol, FromPort, ToPort, CIDR/peer source, and GroupId.
Egress rule schema exposes the corresponding destination dimensions and GroupId.

mappings.preservedMeaning: AWS::EC2::KeyPair can identify SSH key material and accepts PublicKeyMaterial for compute access selection by KeyName.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The resource may represent generated or imported key pairs and its private-material handling and lifecycle are not established by schema shape alone.

evidence.supports: The schema explicitly accepts public key material and names the key pair.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The Instance ImageId property selects a machine image used to instantiate compute.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The scoped inventory has no corresponding managed image resource, and image capture-from-compute semantics are not represented by AWS::EC2::Instance.

evidence.supports: ImageId is a schema candidate for boot-image selection only.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The InstanceType property selects an AWS machine sizing profile for an instance.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The profile is referenced as a property value rather than represented as an independently lifecycle-managed inventory element; detailed capacity semantics are outside this schema packet.

evidence.supports: InstanceType is the schema candidate for reusable machine-size selection.

mappings.preservedMeaning: AWS::EC2::Volume is a lifecycle-managed block-storage resource with capacity and attachment compatibility with instances.

evidence.supports: The volume schema exposes Size, placement, type, and performance properties.

mappings.preservedMeaning: AWS::EC2::VolumeAttachment explicitly connects a VolumeId to an InstanceId and carries the device name.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes VolumeId, InstanceId, and Device as attachment-specific fields.

mappings.preservedMeaning: Instance UserData carries opaque creation-time contextualization data into compute provisioning.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Contextualization is embedded in the instance rather than represented as composable configuration with independent identity, and execution/interpretation behavior is not established by the schema.

evidence.supports: UserData is a schema candidate for creation-time contextualization.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The load-balancer resource can declare Type as network and carries scheme, subnet, address-family, and load-balancer attributes.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The resource type is shared with other Elastic Load Balancing v2 variants, so network-load-balancer identity is a property-selected variant rather than a distinct native element. The neutral aggregate also includes a frontend listener, backend group, and health check; AWS represents those parts separately through Listener and TargetGroup resources rather than through this mapped native ID alone.

evidence.supports: Type is the schema discriminator candidate for a network load balancer.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A Listener is independently declared against LoadBalancerArn and defines the frontend protocol, port, optional certificates, and forwarding actions.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The neutral listener includes its frontend address, but AWS address and subnet selection belongs to the referenced LoadBalancer rather than the Listener resource. The Listener mapping therefore preserves endpoint behavior but not the complete frontend endpoint boundary.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes LoadBalancerArn, Protocol, Port, and DefaultActions.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A TargetGroup is an independently declared backend selection object with target type, target registrations, protocol, port, and VPC placement.

evidence.supports: The schema exposes Targets, TargetType, Protocol, Port, and VpcId.

mappings.preservedMeaning: TargetGroup embeds backend health-check protocol, port, interval, timeout, path, matcher, and healthy/unhealthy thresholds.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: AWS represents the health check as TargetGroup configuration rather than a separately identified or lifecycle-managed resource, and applicable fields vary with target-group protocol.

evidence.supports: HealthCheckProtocol and adjacent HealthCheck* properties are schema candidates for embedded health-check configuration.

providerExtensionAudit.note: The projection covers only neutral hypotheses; the scoped AWS native inventory still requires a separate sample audit for important provider-native concepts absent from the neutral set.

experimentGaps: Measure whether a minimal Docker-on-VM deployment creates or requires explicit NetworkInterface and NetworkInterfaceAttachment resources versus instance-embedded primary networking.
Measure whether block storage attachment is represented explicitly or through instance BlockDeviceMappings in each tested lifecycle path.
Verify NLB Type selection, Listener-to-LoadBalancer wiring, Listener forwarding actions, TargetGroup registration, and embedded health-check behavior with deployed resources.
Verify image, instance type, key material, and user-data runtime requirements and observable lifecycle boundaries; schema candidates alone do not establish necessity.
Audit EC2 Fleet, Spot Fleet, LaunchTemplate, and other scoped native elements as possible AWS extensions without treating them as a neutral compute group absent relational evidence.
